subject: On-prem K8s: cross-rack traffic policy and blockstore pinning
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@opswell.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sabrina.ortiz@opswell.io
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial intake: network egress patterns and PV placement for private cluster

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time last week. We kicked off our internal architecture review and wanted to surface a few constraints before the planning workshop next Wednesday: 

- Multi-rack site: 3 racks, each with its own top-of-rack switch and a dedicated spine aggregation. Cross-rack latency budget ~1ms (we measured ~0.6ms average).
- Egress policy: outbound to third-party inference endpoints must strictly originate from a constrained egress subnet (for IP allowlisting).
- Storage: local NVMe for ephemeral pods (fast cache), and a SAN-backed blockstore for persistent model artifacts. We need a PV placement strategy that avoids cross-rack reads for model pulls during cold start.
- Security: air-gapped management plane; only approved egress for telemetry (mTLS) via a proxy in rack-1.

Can you confirm: 1) recommended nodepool sizing to keep model pulls rack-local, 2) best practice for IP egress anchoring in a private VPC, and 3) whether Redwood Recommend PV classes for the SAN that support snapshot-based rollbacks?

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.png (diagram), pv-class-matrix.xlsx (current in-house PV classes).

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Barnes
Ops Architect, Opswell
alex.barnes@opswell.io
+1 (415) 555-0183
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@opswell.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: network egress patterns and PV placement for private cluster

Alex — thanks for the clear constraints and the diagram. High level notes below; we'll surface the detailed proposal at the workshop but wanted to call out blockers now.

Short answers:
1) Nodepools: use rack-aware nodePoolAffinity — one nodepool per rack for model-serving nodes (gpu-enabled), plus a smaller control/infra nodepool spread across racks for k8s system pods. Start with 6 gpu nodes per rack (g4-equivalent) for predictable warm-cache capacity; scale policy: per-rack autoscaler with cross-rack spillover disabled by default.
2) Egress anchoring: we recommend a NAT gateway pair in rack-1 with SNAT IPs reserved for Redwood telemetry and Opswell inference egress. Use policy routing (ip rule + iptables) on kube-proxies to mark connections from model-serving pods to the egress-subnet — that lets you preserve allowlisted source IPs.
3) PV classes: SAN-backed blockstore should expose two classes: fast-block (rbd/lvm with QoS) for model artifacts and snapshot-enabled slow-block for backups. Redwood runtime supports snapshot restores via CSI snapshotter; we'll document snapshot schedules and retention.

Open questions (please reply inline):
- If cross-rack bandwidth drops below 5 Gbps, are you comfortable with fallback behavior (degraded throughput but keep serving locally)?
- For NTP/time sync we assume an internal stratum-2; can you confirm no public NTP is allowed from compute nodes?
- Do you have any hard retention windows for model artifact snapshots?

I'll loop Karthik to propose the concrete node sizing and a pod-affinity policy we can test in the POC.

Action: Karthik — please draft a rack-aware nodepool template and a simple iptables-based egress anchor proof-of-concept before Monday.

Thanks,
Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
--
From: Sabrina Ortiz <sabrina.ortiz@opswell.io>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@opswell.io>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: network egress patterns and PV placement for private cluster

Hi Vivek — answers below (we pulled these from storage/network teams):

- Cross-rack bandwidth: current switch config guarantees 10 Gbps inter-rack. We can de-prioritize non-critical traffic but want model-serving traffic to have precedence. If throughput falls <5 Gbps we will accept reduced QPS for cold starts but not full failure.
- NTP: compute nodes must use internal stratum-2 only; no outbound NTP to public servers.
- Snapshot retention: critical models (prod) must have 30-day snapshot retention; non-critical (canary/dev) 7 days. Snapshots must be exportable for audits.

We've attached an updated network diagram and our PV-class notes (pv-class-matrix.xlsx). Also, Opswell prefers the egress IPs to be owned by our security team (we can allocate two static IPs for the NAT pair).

Let us know if that helps narrow the design.

Sabrina
Platform Eng, Opswell
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@opswell.io>, sabrina.ortiz@opswell.io
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake: network egress patterns and PV placement for private cluster

Alex / Sabrina — following up with the POC plan and a concise checklist so the workshop is execution-focused. See inline action items and the test matrix.

POC goals (2 weeks):
- Validate egress anchoring with two static IPs and iptables MARK -> SNAT flow for model-serving pods. Test: outbound connection to sandbox endpoint shows static IPs.
- Validate rack-affinity nodepools: one nodepool per rack; schedule model-serving pods with topologySpreadConstraints to prefer same-rack nodes; test: cold-start model pull remains local in 90% of trials.
- Validate CSI snapshot workflow: create snapshot, restore to fast-block class, measure restore time under load.

Checklist for Opswell:
1) Provide 2 static NAT egress IPs and routing rules for rack-1
2) Confirm internal stratum-2 IPs and provide reachability for POC nodes
3) Grant temporary service account to Redwood for CSI snapshotter testing (scoped to PV namespace)

Checklist for Redwood:
1) Deliver nodepool templates and a helm chart that configures node affinity, topologySpread, and a kube-proxy iptables hook for MARKing egress traffic
2) Provide a small Python harness to exercise cold-starts and record model pull locality (we'll deliver metrics to your shared Drive link)

Next steps: schedule a 90-minute workshop week of Nov 8 to run through the checklist and kick off the POC. I'll produce the nodepool templates by Friday (Nov 6).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference
